You are a little confused. When you wire in parallel, you are maintaining the same voltage but are reducing the current for each added cell. In series, the current stays the same as the voltage drops for each cell. The resistance wattage for each cell is always the same regardless, but the total resistance load on the battery is what is changing, and therefore series will drain power more quickly.

Also, in parallel, if a cell is weak, it is naturally supplied less current and as the load turns lessens, the healthier cells slightly charge the weaker ones.

In series it’s a bit the other way around— a weaker cell gets no help from the other cells, and as it gets weaker it’s internal resistance rises and that affects the output voltage.

So in a parallel connection the cells help each other out, and one or more could go completely dead and the others will take up the slack. In a series connection any weak cell just gets weaker and affects the output voltage.

-Electrical Engineer
